questions.s: If f(x) = 3x − 5, then f(4) equals
questions.e: Substitute x = 4: 3(4) − 5 = 12 − 5 = 7. The value 17 comes from adding 5 instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: The sum of the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0 is
questions.e: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the sum of the roots is −b/a = 7 (the roots are 3 and 4). 12 is the product, not the sum.

questions.s: The roots of x² − 6x + 9 = 0 are
questions.e: The discriminant is b² − 4ac = 36 − 36 = 0, so the two roots coincide (x = 3 twice). A positive discriminant would give distinct roots.

questions.s: The value of 5!/3! is
questions.e: 5!/3! = 5 × 4 × 3!/3! = 20. 60 is 5 × 4 × 3, which wrongly leaves part of 3! in the product.

questions.s: The number of ways of choosing 2 objects from 6 distinct objects, ⁶C₂, is
questions.e: ⁶C₂ = (6 × 5)/(2 × 1) = 15. 30 is ⁶P₂, which does not divide by 2!.

questions.s: The value of i⁷, where i² = −1, is
questions.e: i⁴ = 1, so i⁷ = i⁴ · i³ = i³ = i² · i = −i. Choosing i ignores the extra factor of i².

questions.s: The determinant of the matrix with rows (2, 3) and (1, 4) is
questions.e: For rows (a, b) and (c, d) the determinant is ad − bc = 2(4) − 3(1) = 5. 11 results from adding the cross product instead of subtracting.

questions.s: The number of terms in the expansion of (x + y)⁹ is
questions.e: A binomial expansion with index n has n + 1 terms, so 9 + 1 = 10. 9 forgets the term that has no x (or no y).

questions.s: The sum of the first 20 natural numbers is
questions.e: S = n(n + 1)/2 = 20 × 21/2 = 210. 420 is n(n + 1) without halving.

questions.s: The value of log₂ 32 is
questions.e: 32 = 2⁵, so log₂ 32 = 5. 16 comes from dividing 32 by 2 rather than finding the power.

questions.s: The next term of the geometric progression 2, 6, 18, … is
questions.e: The common ratio is 6/2 = 3, so the next term is 18 × 3 = 54. 24 comes from adding 6 to 18 instead of multiplying by the ratio.

questions.s: The product of the roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 is
questions.e: The product of roots is c/a = 3/2. 5/2 is the sum of the roots, −b/a.

questions.s: The transpose of the matrix with rows (1, 2) and (3, 4) has rows
questions.e: Transposing turns rows into columns, so row 1 of the transpose is the first column (1, 3) and row 2 is (2, 4). Swapping the two rows (3, 4) and (1, 2) is not a transpose.

questions.s: The sum to infinity of 1 + ½ + ¼ + … is
questions.e: For |r| < 1, S = a/(1 − r) = 1/(1 − ½) = 2. 4 results from dividing by ½ after using a = 2 by mistake.

questions.s: The coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 + x)⁵ is
questions.e: The coefficient of x² is ⁵C₂ = 10. 5 is ⁵C₁, the coefficient of x.

questions.s: The degree of the polynomial 3x⁴ − 2x + 7 is
questions.e: The degree is the highest power of x, which is 4. 3 is the leading coefficient.

questions.s: The common ratio of the geometric progression 4, −2, 1, … is
questions.e: The ratio is the second term divided by the first: −2/4 = −½. Dividing in the wrong order gives −2.

questions.s: The number of ways of choosing all 8 objects from 8 distinct objects, ⁸C₈, is
questions.e: ⁸C₈ = 8!/(8! · 0!) = 1, because exactly one way exists to choose all 8 objects. 0 would suggest that no selection is possible.

questions.s: The quadratic equation whose roots are 2 and −3 is
questions.e: Sum of roots = −1 and product = −6, so the equation is x² − (sum)x + product = x² + x − 6 = 0. Writing x² − x − 6 uses the sum with the wrong sign.

questions.s: For which values of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?
questions.e: Equal roots need k² − 4(9) = 0, so k² = 36 and k = ±6. ±3 comes from setting k² = 9.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0, then α² + β² equals
questions.e: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 25 − 6 = 19. 22 or 28 arise from using −3 or +3 instead of 2αβ = 6.

questions.s: A geometric progression has third term 12 and sixth term 96. Its first term is
questions.e: Dividing, r³ = 96/12 = 8, so r = 2. Then ar² = 12 gives a = 12/4 = 3. Taking a = 6 treats the third term as ar.

questions.s: The number of different arrangements of all the letters of the word LAHORE is
questions.e: All six letters are different, so there are 6! = 720 arrangements. 360 would be right only if two letters were repeated.

questions.s: The number of different arrangements of the letters of the word BILAL is
questions.e: Five letters with L repeated twice give 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60. 120 ignores the repetition.

questions.s: A committee of 3 is chosen from 5 men and 4 women so that it has at least one woman. The number of ways is
questions.e: Subtract the all-men committees from all committees: ⁹C₃ − ⁵C₃ = 84 − 10 = 74. 112 comes from choosing one woman first and then any 2 of the other 8, which counts some committees more than once.

questions.s: The middle term in the expansion of (x + 2)⁶ is
questions.e: With 7 terms the middle one is the 4th: ⁶C₃ x³ 2³ = 20 × 8 x³ = 160x³. 20x³ forgets the power of 2.

questions.s: The coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2 + x)⁵ is
questions.e: The term is ⁵C₃ · 2² · x³ = 10 × 4 x³ = 40x³. 80 uses 2³ instead of 2² by mistake.

questions.s: The inverse of f(x) = (x + 3)/2 is f⁻¹(x) =
questions.e: Write y = (x + 3)/2, so x = 2y − 3; swapping gives f⁻¹(x) = 2x − 3. 2x + 3 forgets to subtract 3 when undoing the addition.

questions.s: The determinant of the 3 × 3 matrix with rows (1, 2, 0), (0, 1, 3) and (2, 0, 1) is
questions.e: Expanding along row 1: 1(1·1 − 3·0) − 2(0·1 − 3·2) + 0 = 1 − 2(−6) = 13. −11 comes from dropping the negative sign of the minor.

questions.s: The solutions of 2x² − 5x − 3 = 0 are
questions.e: Factorise: (2x + 1)(x − 3) = 0, so x = −½ or x = 3. x = ½ comes from a sign slip in the first factor.

questions.s: The sum of the first 12 odd natural numbers is
questions.e: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n², so 12² = 144. 156 is 12 × 13, the sum of the first 12 even numbers.

questions.s: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, the value of log₁₀ 5 is
questions.e: 5 = 10/2, so log 5 = 1 − log 2 = 1 − 0.3010 = 0.6990. 1.5050 multiplies 0.3010 by 5, which does not apply to logarithms.

questions.s: The roots of x² − 4x + 13 = 0 are
questions.e: x = [4 ± √(16 − 52)]/2 = (4 ± 6i)/2 = 2 ± 3i. 2 ± 6i forgets to halve the imaginary part.

questions.s: In (3x + 5)/((x + 1)(x + 2)) = A/(x + 1) + B/(x + 2), the values of A and B are
questions.e: Put x = −1: A = (−3 + 5)/(1) = 2. Put x = −2: B = (−6 + 5)/(−1) = 1. Swapping the values suggests a mix-up of which factor was removed.

questions.s: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, the value of (1 + ω²)³ is
questions.e: Since 1 + ω + ω² = 0, 1 + ω² = −ω. Then (−ω)³ = −ω³ = −1. The answer 1 forgets the negative sign.

questions.s: The number of diagonals of a hexagon is
questions.e: n(n − 3)/2 = 6(3)/2 = 9. 15 is ⁶C₂, which counts the sides as well.

questions.s: The remainder when x³ − 2x² + x − 5 is divided by x − 2 is
questions.e: By the remainder theorem, substitute x = 2: 8 − 8 + 2 − 5 = −3. −5 is the value at x = 0, the constant term.

questions.s: If x − 2 is a factor of x³ + kx² + x − 6, then k equals
questions.e: p(2) = 8 + 4k + 2 − 6 = 4k + 4 = 0, so k = −1. k = 1 results from a sign error in the constant term.

questions.s: If A has rows (1, 2) and (3, 4), and B has rows (0, 1) and (1, 0), then AB has rows
questions.e: Multiplying A by B swaps the columns of A: row (1, 2) becomes (2, 1) and (3, 4) becomes (4, 3). (3, 4) and (1, 2) is BA, which swaps rows instead.

questions.s: In how many ways can 5 people sit around a circular table?
questions.e: Fixing one person to remove rotations leaves 4! = 24 arrangements. 120 treats the seats as distinguishable, as for a row.

questions.s: The sum to infinity of the geometric series 6 − 3 + 3/2 − … is
questions.e: a = 6 and r = −½, so S = 6/(1 + ½) = 4. 12 results from using r = ½ and then dividing by it.

questions.s: The harmonic mean of 2 and 6 is
questions.e: H = 2ab/(a + b) = 2(2)(6)/8 = 3. 4 is the arithmetic mean and 2√3 is the geometric mean.

questions.s: The range of f(x) = x² + 1, where x is real, is
questions.e: x² ≥ 0 for all real x, so x² + 1 ≥ 1, with the minimum 1 at x = 0. y ≥ 0 is the range of x², not x² + 1.

questions.s: Which of these functions is one-to-one on all real numbers?
questions.e: x³ is strictly increasing, so different inputs give different outputs. x² and |x| give the same value at x and −x, and sin x repeats every 2π.

questions.s: If ⁿC₂ = 45, then n equals
questions.e: n(n − 1)/2 = 45 gives n² − n − 90 = 0, so (n − 10)(n + 9) = 0 and n = 10. 9 gives ⁹C₂ = 36.

questions.s: If A has rows (1, 1) and (1, 0), then A² has rows
questions.e: Row 1 × A: (1·1 + 1·1, 1·1 + 1·0) = (2, 1). Row 2: (1·1 + 0, 1·1 + 0) = (1, 1). Squaring each entry separately gives (1, 1) and (1, 0), which is wrong.

questions.s: The solution of x² − x − 12 ≤ 0 is
questions.e: x² − x − 12 = (x − 4)(x + 3), which is ≤ 0 between the roots, so −3 ≤ x ≤ 4. 'x ≤ −3 or x ≥ 4' is the solution of the opposite inequality.

questions.s: The sum of the squares of the first 10 natural numbers is
questions.e: n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 10 × 11 × 21/6 = 385. 3,025 is the sum of cubes, and 55 is the sum of the numbers themselves.

questions.s: If the roots of x² − 7x + k = 0 differ by 3, then k equals
questions.e: Roots a and a + 3 with sum 7 give a = 2, so the roots are 2 and 5 and k = 10. 12 corresponds to roots 3 and 4, which differ by only 1.

questions.s: If α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0, then α³ + β³ equals
questions.e: α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β) = 27 − 3(1)(3) = 18. 24 subtracts only 3 instead of 3αβ(α + β) = 9.
Σk(k + 1) = n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = 10 × 11 × 12/3 = 440. 385 is only Σk², missing the Σk part.

questions.s: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of MATHEMATICS is
questions.e: There are 11 letters with M, A and T each repeated twice, so 11!/(2! 2! 2!) = 39,916,800/8 = 4,989,600. Dividing by only one or two of the repeats gives the other options.

questions.s: The letters of EQUATION are arranged so that all five vowels come together. The number of arrangements is
questions.e: Treat the vowels as one block: 4 units (block, Q, T, N) give 4! = 24, and the vowels inside can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways, so 24 × 120 = 2,880. 14,400 treats the consonants as 5 units.

questions.s: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 4, then |2A| equals
questions.e: Multiplying every row by 2 multiplies the determinant by 2³ = 8, so |2A| = 32. 8 multiplies the determinant by 2 only once, and 16 applies 2² as if A were 2 × 2.

questions.s: The inverse of the matrix with rows (2, 1) and (5, 3) has rows
questions.e: The determinant is 6 − 5 = 1. The inverse swaps the diagonal entries and negates the others: rows (3, −1) and (−5, 2). Leaving the off-diagonal entries positive gives a matrix whose product with A is not the identity.

questions.s: The solution of log₂ x + log₂ (x − 2) = 3 is
questions.e: Combining, x(x − 2) = 8, so x² − 2x − 8 = 0 and x = 4 or −2. Logarithms need positive arguments, so x = −2 is rejected and x = 4.

questions.s: The solutions of |x − 2| + |x + 1| = 5 are
questions.e: For x ≥ 2: 2x − 1 = 5 gives x = 3. For x ≤ −1: −2x + 1 = 5 gives x = −2. Between −1 and 2 the sum is always 3, so no solution there; both x = −2 and x = 3 work.

questions.s: If one root of x² + kx + 6 = 0 is double the other, then k equals
questions.e: Roots a and 2a give product 2a² = 6, so a = ±√3, and the sum 3a = ±3√3 equals −k. ±3 results from using a = ±1 and ignoring the product condition.

questions.s: A group of 4 is selected from 6 boys and 5 girls so that it has at least 2 girls. The number of ways is
questions.e: Total ¹¹C₄ = 330, minus no girls ⁶C₄ = 15, minus exactly one girl 5 × ⁶C₃ = 100, giving 215. 150 counts only the case of exactly 2 girls and 2 boys.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of a progression is Sₙ = 3n² + 2n. Its common difference is
questions.e: a₁ = S₁ = 5 and a₂ = S₂ − S₁ = 16 − 5 = 11, so d = 11 − 5 = 6. 5 is the first term, not the difference.

questions.s: The 10th term of the arithmetic progression 5, 8, 11, … is
questions.e: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d = 5 + 9(3) = 32. 35 is the 11th term, which results from using n instead of n − 1 as the multiplier.

questions.s: The domain of f(x) = √(x − 2) over the real numbers is
questions.e: The expression under the root must be non-negative, so x − 2 ≥ 0, giving x ≥ 2. At x = 2 the value is 0, which is defined, so x > 2 is too strict.

questions.s: The solutions of |x − 3| = 5 are
questions.e: |x − 3| = 5 means x − 3 = 5 or x − 3 = −5, so x = 8 or x = −2. Taking only the positive case misses the second solution.

questions.s: The sum of the first 15 terms of the progression 3, 7, 11, … is
questions.e: With a = 3 and d = 4, S₁₅ = (15/2)[2(3) + 14(4)] = 7.5 × 62 = 465. 930 results from forgetting the factor ½.

questions.s: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², then f(g(3)) equals
questions.e: First g(3) = 9, then f(9) = 2(9) + 1 = 19. 49 is g(f(3)), the composition in the opposite order.

questions.s: The solution set of |2x − 1| < 5 is
questions.e: −5 < 2x − 1 < 5 gives −4 < 2x < 6, so −2 < x < 3. −3 < x < 2 comes from adding 1 to both sides of the wrong inequality.

questions.s: The sum of the squares of all the roots of x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 is
questions.e: Factorising, (x² − 1)(x² − 4) = 0, so the roots are ±1 and ±2. The squares sum to 1 + 1 + 4 + 4 = 10. 5 counts each pair only once.

questions.s: The sum of the coefficients in the expansion of (2x − 1)⁴ is
questions.e: Put x = 1: (2 − 1)⁴ = 1. 16 would be the sum of the absolute values only if all signs were positive, which is not the case here.

questions.s: The term independent of x in the expansion of (x² + 1/x)⁹ is
questions.e: The general term ⁹Cᵣ x^(18−2r) x^(−r) has power 18 − 3r, which is 0 when r = 6, so the term is ⁹C₆ = 84. 126 is ⁹C₄, from a wrong power count.
Each term 1/(k(k + 1)) = 1/k − 1/(k + 1), so the sum telescopes to 1 − 1/10 = 9/10. 10/11 would correspond to ten terms.

questions.s: The value of sin 30° is
questions.e: sin 30° = ½ from the standard 30°–60°–90° triangle. √3/2 is sin 60°, the value for the other acute angle.

questions.s: An angle of 135° equals how many radians?
If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, then cos θ equals
questions.e: cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ) = √(1 − 9/25) = 4/5. 3/4 is tan θ, the ratio of the two known sides.

questions.s: The period of the function y = sin 2x is
questions.e: The period of sin(bx) is 2π/b = 2π/2 = π. 2π is the period of sin x without the factor 2.

questions.s: sin(90° + θ) is equal to
questions.e: Shifting the sine curve by 90° to the left gives the cosine curve, so sin(90° + θ) = cos θ. −cos θ would be sin(θ − 90°).

questions.s: An angle of 5π/6 radians equals
The length of the arc of a circle of radius 6 cm that subtends an angle of π/3 radians at the centre is
questions.e: Arc length s = rθ = 6 × π/3 = 2π cm. 6π cm multiplies the radius by π instead of by the angle.

questions.s: If sin θ is positive and tan θ is negative, the angle θ lies in the
questions.e: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II. Tangent is positive in I and III, so it is negative only in II among those two. In the first quadrant every ratio is positive.

questions.s: 1 + tan²θ is equal to
questions.e: Dividing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ gives tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ. cosec²θ pairs with 1 + cot²θ.

questions.s: The domain of the function sin⁻¹x is
questions.e: The sine of any angle lies between −1 and 1, so only these x have an inverse sine. −π/2 ≤ x ≤ π/2 is the range of sin⁻¹x, not its domain.

questions.s: The principal value of sin⁻¹(½) is
questions.e: sin(π/6) = ½ and π/6 lies in [−π/2, π/2]. 5π/6 also has sine ½ but is outside the principal range.

questions.s: The value of sin 75° is
If sin θ = 1/3, then cos 2θ equals
questions.e: cos 2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ = 1 − 2/9 = 7/9. 8/9 is cos²θ, and 1/9 is sin²θ; neither is cos 2θ.

questions.s: The solutions of sin θ = ½ for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π are
questions.e: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II, giving θ = π/6 and π − π/6 = 5π/6. 7π/6 and 11π/6 lie in the quadrants where sine is negative.

questions.s: For 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, the solutions of tan θ = −1 are
questions.e: The tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV, with reference angle π/4: θ = π − π/4 = 3π/4 and 2π − π/4 = 7π/4. π/4 and 5π/4 are the solutions of tan θ = +1.

questions.s: In a triangle ABC, a = 10, ∠A = 30° and ∠B = 45°. The side b equals
questions.e: By the sine rule b = a sin B/sin A = 10(√2/2)/(½) = 10√2. 5√2 results from inverting the ratio of sines.

questions.s: Two sides of a triangle are 5 cm and 8 cm and the angle between them is 60°. The third side is
questions.e: By the cosine rule c² = 25 + 64 − 2(5)(8)cos 60° = 89 − 40 = 49, so c = 7. √89 forgets the cosine term and √129 adds it.

questions.s: The area of a triangle with two sides of 6 cm and 8 cm and the included angle 30° is
questions.e: Area = ½ab sin C = ½(6)(8)(½) = 12 cm². 24 omits the ½ of the formula, and 12√3 uses sin 60° instead of sin 30°.

questions.s: From a point 20 m from the foot of a pole on level ground, the angle of elevation of its top is 60°. The height of the pole is
questions.e: tan 60° = height/20, so height = 20√3 ≈ 34.6 m. 20/√3 uses tan 30° by mistake.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(sin 5π/6) is
questions.e: sin(5π/6) = ½, and the principal value of sin⁻¹(½) lies in [−π/2, π/2], so the result is π/6. 5π/6 lies outside the principal range.

questions.s: The value of cos(sin⁻¹ 3/5) is
questions.e: Let θ = sin⁻¹(3/5); in the right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 5 and opposite side 3, the adjacent side is 4, so cos θ = 4/5. 3/4 is tan θ.

questions.s: The expression sin 2θ/(1 + cos 2θ) simplifies to
questions.e: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and 1 + cos 2θ = 2cos²θ, so the ratio is sin θ/cos θ = tan θ. 2 tan θ comes from losing the factor 2 in the denominator.

questions.s: The general solution of cos 2x = 0 is
questions.e: cos 2x = 0 gives 2x = (2n + 1)π/2, so x = (2n + 1)π/4. nπ/4 would include even multiples of π/4 such as x = 0, where cos 2x = 1.

questions.s: The minimum value of 2 − 3 cos x is
questions.e: cos x ranges over [−1, 1], so −3 cos x ranges over [−3, 3], and 2 − 3cos x has minimum 2 − 3 = −1. −3 forgets the constant 2.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 10 cm has a central angle of 72°. Its area is
questions.e: 72° = 2π/5 radians, so area = ½r²θ = ½(100)(2π/5) = 20π cm². 40π omits the ½.

questions.s: If sin A = 3/5 and cos B = 5/13, with A and B both acute, then sin(A + B) equals
The number of solutions of tan x = 1 in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 4π is
questions.e: The tangent has period π and tan x = 1 first at x = π/4, so the solutions are π/4, 5π/4, 9π/4 and 13π/4. 2 counts only one period of 2π.

questions.s: The value of tan⁻¹(½) + tan⁻¹(⅓) is
questions.e: tan⁻¹a + tan⁻¹b = tan⁻¹[(a + b)/(1 − ab)] = tan⁻¹[(5/6)/(5/6)] = tan⁻¹1 = π/4. tan⁻¹(5/6) forgets the denominator.

questions.s: In a triangle with sides 4, 5 and 6, the cosine of the largest angle is
questions.e: The largest angle is opposite the side 6: cos C = (4² + 5² − 6²)/(2·4·5) = 5/40 = 1/8. 3/4 is the cosine of the smallest angle, opposite 4.

questions.s: The expression sin(π − θ) cos(π/2 − θ) simplifies to
questions.e: sin(π − θ) = sin θ and cos(π/2 − θ) = sin θ, so the product is sin²θ. sin θ cos θ would need one factor to become cos θ.

questions.s: The value of tan 15° is
The expression (sin θ + cos θ)² is equal to
questions.e: (sin θ + cos θ)² = sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ = 1 + sin 2θ. 1 − sin 2θ is the expansion of (sin θ − cos θ)².

questions.s: The solutions of sin x + cos x = 1 for 0 ≤ x < 2π are
questions.e: Squaring gives 1 + sin 2x = 1, so sin 2x = 0 and x = 0, π/2, π, 3π/2. Checking the original equation, only 0 and π/2 work; at π and 3π/2 the sum is −1, an extraneous result of squaring.

questions.s: The solutions of 2 sin²x + 3 cos x = 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π are
questions.e: Using sin²x = 1 − cos²x: 2cos²x − 3cos x − 2 = 0, so (2cos x + 1)(cos x − 2) = 0. cos x = 2 is impossible, so cos x = −½ and x = 2π/3, 4π/3.

questions.s: If A + B = 45°, then (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) equals
questions.e: tan(A + B) = 1 gives tan A + tan B = 1 − tan A tan B. Then (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 1 + (tan A + tan B) + tan A tan B = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.s: The value of sin⁻¹(3/5) + sin⁻¹(4/5) is
questions.e: Let α = sin⁻¹(3/5); then cos α = 4/5, so sin⁻¹(4/5) = π/2 − α. The two angles are the acute angles of a 3–4–5 triangle and add up to 90°, that is π/2.

questions.s: For x = 1/5, the value of cos(2 cos⁻¹x + sin⁻¹x) is
questions.e: Since sin⁻¹x = π/2 − cos⁻¹x, the angle equals cos⁻¹x + π/2 and cos(θ + π/2) = −sin θ. With θ = cos⁻¹(1/5), sin θ = √(1 − 1/25) = 2√6/5, so the value is −2√6/5.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, a = 2, b = √6 and ∠A = 45°. The possible values of ∠B are
questions.e: sin B = b sin A/a = √6(√2/2)/2 = √3/2, so B = 60° or 120°. Both are allowed because a < b and 45° + 120° < 180°, the ambiguous case. Considering only 60° ignores the obtuse solution.

questions.s: The solutions of sin 2x = sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π are
questions.e: 2 sin x cos x − sin x = 0 gives sin x (2 cos x − 1) = 0, so sin x = 0 (x = 0, π) or cos x = ½ (x = π/3). Dividing by sin x loses the solutions 0 and π.

questions.s: The minimum value of sec²x + cosec²x is
questions.e: sec²x + cosec²x = 1/(sin²x cos²x) = 4/sin²2x. Since sin²2x ≤ 1, the minimum is 4, reached at x = π/4. 2 arises from adding the minimum values of sec² and cosec² separately, which cannot occur together.

questions.s: The value of tan 45° is
questions.e: At 45° the opposite and adjacent sides of the right-angled isosceles triangle are equal, so tan 45° = 1. 1/√3 is tan 30°.

questions.s: sin(−θ) is equal to
questions.e: Sine is an odd function: reflecting the angle about the x-axis changes the sign of the sine. Cosine, by contrast, is even.

questions.s: The principal value of cos⁻¹(0) is
questions.e: cos(π/2) = 0 and π/2 lies in [0, π]. cos 0 = 1, so 0 is not the angle.

questions.s: If tan A = ½ and tan B = ⅓, then tan(A + B) equals
questions.e: tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B) = (5/6)/(1 − 1/6) = 1. 5/6 forgets the denominator; 5/7 uses 1 + tan A tan B.

questions.s: The period of the function y = tan 3x is
questions.e: tan(bx) has period π/b = π/3. 2π/3 wrongly uses the period of sine and cosine.

questions.s: The maximum value of 3 sin x + 4 cos x is
questions.e: a sin x + b cos x has maximum √(a² + b²) = √(9 + 16) = 5. 7 adds the two coefficients as if both could peak together.

questions.s: The principal value of cos⁻¹(−½) is
questions.e: cos⁻¹ takes values in [0, π]. cos(π/3) = ½, so the angle with cosine −½ is π − π/3 = 2π/3. 4π/3 has the right cosine but lies outside [0, π].

questions.s: If cot θ = 3/4 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then sin θ equals
questions.e: cot θ = cos θ/sin θ = 3/4 gives sides 3 and 4 with hypotenuse 5. In the third quadrant both sine and cosine are negative, so sin θ = −4/5. 3/5 is the magnitude of the cosine.

questions.s: The value of sin 10° sin 50° sin 70° is
questions.e: Use the identity sin θ sin(60° − θ) sin(60° + θ) = ¼ sin 3θ with θ = 10°: the product is ¼ sin 30° = 1/8. 1/4 forgets that sin 30° = ½.

questions.s: The value of cos 36° cos 72° is
questions.e: Multiply and divide by sin 36° and use sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A twice: cos36° cos72° = sin 144°/(4 sin 36°) = 1/4, because sin 144° = sin 36°. 1/2 would result from applying the double-angle step only once.

questions.s: The limit of x² + 3x as x approaches 2 is
questions.e: The function is continuous, so substitute x = 2: 4 + 6 = 10. 8 would result from adding 4 + 4 instead of 3x = 6.

questions.s: The derivative of x⁵ with respect to x is
questions.e: By the power rule d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹, so the derivative is 5x⁴. 4x⁵ lowers the power but multiplies by the wrong number.

questions.s: The derivative of sin x is
questions.e: d/dx(sin x) = cos x. −sin x is the derivative of cos x.

questions.s: The derivative of eˣ is
questions.e: The exponential function is its own derivative. x eˣ⁻¹ wrongly applies the power rule, which is only for a variable base and constant power.

questions.s: The integral ∫ cos x dx equals
questions.e: Since d/dx(sin x) = cos x, the integral is sin x + C. −sin x is the derivative of cos x.

questions.s: The limit of (sin x)/x as x → 0, with x in radians, is
questions.e: This is a standard limit: sin x ≈ x for small x measured in radians, so the ratio tends to 1. Substituting x = 0 gives 0/0, which is not by itself an answer.

questions.s: The derivative of ln x is
questions.e: d/dx(ln x) = 1/x for x > 0. 1/ln x inverts the function instead of differentiating it.

questions.s: The slope of the tangent to the curve y = x² at the point where x = 3 is
questions.e: The slope is dy/dx = 2x, which is 6 at x = 3. 9 is the y-coordinate of the point, not the slope.

questions.s: The derivative of the constant function f(x) = 7 is
questions.e: A constant function has a horizontal graph, so its rate of change is 0 everywhere. 7 confuses the value of the function with its derivative.

questions.s: The derivative of cos x is
questions.e: d/dx(cos x) = −sin x. Writing +sin x loses the negative sign.

questions.s: The integral ∫ (1/x) dx, for x > 0, equals
questions.e: Since d/dx(ln x) = 1/x, the integral is ln x + C. −1/x² is the derivative of 1/x, so it goes the wrong way.

questions.s: The derivative of 3x² − 4x + 1 is
questions.e: Differentiate term by term: 6x − 4 + 0. 6x + 4 loses the sign of the middle term.

questions.s: The limit of 1/x as x → ∞ is
questions.e: As x grows without bound, 1/x becomes arbitrarily small and positive, so the limit is 0. ∞ would be the limit of x, not 1/x.

questions.s: A differentiable function f is increasing on an interval where f′(x) is
questions.e: A positive derivative means the function value rises as x increases. A negative derivative means it is decreasing.

questions.s: The derivative of √x is
questions.e: Write √x = x^(½), so the derivative is ½ x^(−½) = 1/(2√x). 2√x multiplies instead of dividing by 2.

questions.s: The derivative of tan x is
questions.e: d/dx(tan x) = sec²x. cosec²x appears in the derivative of −cot x, and sec x tan x is the derivative of sec x.

questions.s: The limit of (x² − 9)/(x − 3) as x → 3 is
questions.e: Factorise: (x − 3)(x + 3)/(x − 3) = x + 3 for x ≠ 3, whose limit is 6. Direct substitution gives 0/0, which does not mean the limit is 0.

questions.s: The value of the definite integral of 2x from x = 1 to x = 3 is
questions.e: [x²] from 1 to 3 = 9 − 1 = 8. 9 forgets to subtract the value at the lower limit.

questions.s: The derivative of x² sin x is
questions.e: The product rule gives (2x)(sin x) + (x²)(cos x). 2x cos x differentiates both factors at once, which is wrong.

questions.s: The derivative of (x² + 1)/(x − 1) at x = 2 is
questions.e: By the quotient rule, [2x(x − 1) − (x² + 1)]/(x − 1)² = (4 − 5)/1 = −1. Reversing the numerator terms gives +1.

questions.s: The derivative of sin(3x²) is
questions.e: By the chain rule, cos(3x²) multiplied by the derivative of the inner function 6x. 3 cos(3x²) uses the wrong inner derivative.

questions.s: The integral ∫ (3x² + 2x − 1) dx equals
questions.e: Integrate term by term: 3x² → x³, 2x → x², −1 → −x. 6x + 2 is the derivative of the integrand.

questions.s: The integral ∫ sin 2x dx equals
questions.e: The integral of sin u is −cos u, and dividing by the inner derivative 2 gives −½ cos 2x. Without the ½ the derivative would be 2 sin 2x.

questions.s: The value of the integral of cos x from 0 to π/2 is
questions.e: [sin x] from 0 to π/2 = 1 − 0 = 1. −1 reverses the limits.

questions.s: The limit of (1 − cos x)/x² as x → 0 is
questions.e: Use 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2): the ratio is 2 sin²(x/2)/x² = ½ (sin(x/2)/(x/2))², which tends to ½. 0 arises from reading the limit as 0/0 = 0.

questions.s: The limit of (3x² + 2x)/(x² + 5) as x → ∞ is
questions.e: Dividing numerator and denominator by x² leaves (3 + 2/x)/(1 + 5/x²) → 3. 0 would be right only if the denominator had a higher power than the numerator.

questions.s: The equation of the tangent to y = x³ − 2x at the point (1, −1) is
questions.e: The slope is 3x² − 2 = 1 at x = 1, so y + 1 = 1(x − 1), i.e. y = x − 2. y = 3x − 4 uses the slope 3x² = 3 and forgets the −2.

questions.s: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 m. The greatest possible area is
questions.e: With sides x and 20 − x, A = x(20 − x), which is greatest at x = 10, giving 100 m² (a square). 400 m² is 20², the square of the semi-perimeter.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local maximum at
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1, and f″(x) = 6x is negative at x = −1, so that is a maximum. At x = 1 the second derivative is positive, giving a minimum.

questions.s: The area under the curve y = x² between x = 0 and x = 3 is
questions.e: [x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 27/3 = 9. 27 forgets to divide by 3.

questions.s: The integral ∫ x e^(x²) dx equals
questions.e: Put u = x², du = 2x dx, so x dx = du/2 and the integral is ½ eᵘ + C. Without the factor ½ the derivative would be 2x e^(x²).

questions.s: The integral ∫ 2x/(x² + 1) dx equals
questions.e: The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so the integral is ln(x² + 1) + C. tan⁻¹x is the integral of 1/(x² + 1).

questions.s: The derivative of ln(x² + 1) is
questions.e: By the chain rule: (1/(x² + 1)) · 2x. Writing only 1/(x² + 1) forgets the derivative of the inner function.

questions.s: The function f(x) = |x| at x = 0 is
questions.e: The left-hand slope is −1 and the right-hand slope is +1, so the two one-sided derivatives differ and f′(0) does not exist. The graph has a sharp corner there even though it is continuous.

questions.s: The integral ∫ x cos x dx equals
o: x sin x + cos x + C
x sin x − cos x + C
questions.e: By parts with u = x, dv = cos x dx: x sin x − ∫ sin x dx = x sin x + cos x + C. x sin x − cos x results from integrating sin x with the wrong sign.

questions.s: The value of the integral of 1/x from x = 1 to x = e is
questions.e: [ln x] from 1 to e = ln e − ln 1 = 1 − 0 = 1. e − 1 would result from integrating the constant 1 instead of 1/x.

questions.s: The radius of a circle increases at 2 cm/s. When the radius is 5 cm, the area is increasing at the rate of
questions.e: A = πr², so dA/dt = 2πr (dr/dt) = 2π(5)(2) = 20π cm²/s. 50π results from using 2π r² instead of 2π r (dr/dt).

questions.s: The edge of a cube is increasing at 3 cm/s. When the edge is 4 cm, the volume is increasing at
questions.e: V = x³, so dV/dt = 3x²(dx/dt) = 3(16)(3) = 144 cm³/s. 48 forgets the factor dx/dt = 3.

questions.s: If dy/dx = 2x and y = 1 when x = 0, then y equals
questions.e: Integrating gives y = x² + C, and y(0) = 1 gives C = 1. Dropping the constant gives x², which fails the condition.

questions.s: The second derivative of x⁴ − 3x² is
questions.e: First derivative 4x³ − 6x, second derivative 12x² − 6. 4x³ − 6x is only the first derivative.

questions.s: The curve y = x³ − 6x² + 9x has a point of inflection at
questions.e: y″ = 6x − 12 = 0 at x = 2, and it changes sign there. x = 1 and x = 3 are the stationary points where y′ = 0.

questions.s: The area enclosed between the curves y = x and y = x² is
questions.e: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1, with y = x above. Area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = ½ − ⅓ = 1/6. 1/3 is the area under y = x² alone.

questions.s: Differentiating the square of the cosine function, cos²x, gives
questions.e: By the chain rule, 2 cos x (−sin x) = −2 sin x cos x = −sin 2x. −2 cos x forgets the factor from the derivative of cos x.

questions.s: The derivative of the inverse tangent function, tan⁻¹x, is
questions.e: This standard result follows from y = tan⁻¹x ⇒ x = tan y ⇒ dx/dy = sec²y = 1 + x². 1/√(1 − x²) is the derivative of sin⁻¹x.

questions.s: The integral ∫ dx/√(1 − x²) equals
questions.e: Since d/dx(sin⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 − x²), the integral is sin⁻¹x + C. tan⁻¹x is the integral of 1/(1 + x²).

questions.s: The derivative of sin⁻¹(2x) is
questions.e: By the chain rule, 1/√(1 − (2x)²) × 2 = 2/√(1 − 4x²). Without the factor 2 the inner derivative is lost.

questions.s: At the point (3, 4) on the circle x² + y² = 25, the slope dy/dx is
questions.e: Differentiating implicitly, 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = −x/y = −3/4. −4/3 inverts the ratio.

questions.s: For x > 0, the derivative of xˣ is
questions.e: Take logarithms: ln y = x ln x, so y′/y = ln x + 1 and y′ = xˣ(1 + ln x). x · xˣ⁻¹ treats the exponent as constant, and xˣ ln x treats the base as constant.

questions.s: The limit of (tan x − sin x)/x³ as x → 0 is
questions.e: tan x − sin x = tan x (1 − cos x). Dividing by x³ gives (tan x/x)((1 − cos x)/x²) → 1 × ½ = ½. The answer 0 comes from stopping at 0/0.

questions.s: The limit of (1 + 2/x)ˣ as x → ∞ is
questions.e: Write (1 + 2/x)ˣ = [(1 + 2/x)^(x/2)]², and the bracket tends to e, so the limit is e². Answer e treats the 2 as if it were 1.

questions.s: The value of the integral of sin³x from 0 to π/2 is
questions.e: Write sin³x = sin x (1 − cos²x) and put u = cos x: the integral becomes ∫₀¹ (1 − u²) du = 1 − ⅓ = 2/3. 1/3 forgets the first term.

questions.s: An open box is made from a square sheet of side 12 cm by cutting equal squares of side x from the corners and folding up the sides. The greatest possible volume is
questions.e: V = x(12 − 2x)², V′ = (12 − 2x)(12 − 6x) = 0 gives x = 2 (x = 6 gives zero volume). V(2) = 2 × 64 = 128 cm³. 108 is the volume at x = 3, which is not the maximum.

questions.s: The area enclosed between the curve y = x² and the line y = 4 is
questions.e: They meet at x = ±2. Area = ∫₋₂² (4 − x²) dx = 16 − 16/3 = 32/3. 16/3 is half of this, from integrating only from 0 to 2.

questions.s: The integral ∫ x² ln x dx equals
questions.e: By parts with u = ln x, dv = x² dx: (x³/3) ln x − ∫ (x³/3)(1/x) dx = (x³/3) ln x − x³/9 + C. Forgetting the extra 1/3 from integrating x² gives −x³/3.

questions.s: The integral ∫ dx/(x² − 1), for x > 1, equals
questions.e: Partial fractions: 1/(x² − 1) = ½[1/(x − 1) − 1/(x + 1)], so the integral is ½[ln(x − 1) − ln(x + 1)] + C. Inverting the fraction reverses the sign.

questions.s: The region under y = x from x = 0 to x = 3 is rotated about the x-axis. The volume of the solid formed is
questions.e: V = π∫₀³ y² dx = π[x³/3]₀³ = 9π. 27π forgets to divide by 3 after integrating x².

questions.s: The curve y = ax² + bx passes through the point (1, 2) and has gradient 4 there. The values of a and b are
questions.e: The point gives a + b = 2 and the gradient 2ax + b = 4 gives 2a + b = 4. Subtracting, a = 2 and b = 0. a = 1, b = 1 satisfies the point but has gradient 3.

questions.s: The value of the integral of x/(1 + x²) from x = 0 to x = 1 is
questions.e: The integral is ½[ln(1 + x²)] from 0 to 1 = ½ ln 2. ln 2 forgets the factor ½ that comes from d(x²) = 2x dx.

questions.s: The limit of (x − sin x)/x³ as x → 0 is
questions.e: Applying L'Hôpital's rule three times (or using sin x ≈ x − x³/6) gives (x³/6)/x³ = 1/6. 1/3 comes from stopping after two differentiations without the final division by 3 × 2.

questions.s: The solution of dy/dx = y with y = 2 when x = 0 is
questions.e: Separating variables, ln y = x + c, so y = Aeˣ, and y(0) = 2 gives A = 2. y = eˣ + 1 gives y(0) = 2 but dy/dx = eˣ ≠ y.

questions.s: The integral ∫ x³ dx equals
questions.e: Add 1 to the power and divide by the new power: x⁴/4 + C. 3x² is the derivative of x³, not its integral.

questions.s: The value of the definite integral of x from 0 to 2 is
questions.e: [x²/2] from 0 to 2 is 4/2 − 0 = 2. 4 forgets to divide by 2.

questions.s: The integral ∫ eˣ dx equals
questions.e: The derivative of eˣ is eˣ, so its integral is eˣ + C. xeˣ differentiates to eˣ + xeˣ, which is not eˣ.

questions.s: Differentiating the exponential function e²ˣ with respect to x gives
questions.e: The chain rule multiplies eᵘ by u′ = 2. e²ˣ/2 is the integral, not the derivative.

questions.s: The minimum value of f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 is
questions.e: f′(x) = 2x − 6 = 0 gives x = 3 and f(3) = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4. 3 is the position of the minimum, not its value.

questions.s: A particle moves so that its displacement is s = t³ − 6t² + 9t metres at time t seconds. Its velocity is zero at t = 1 and t = 3. The acceleration at t = 3 s is
questions.e: a = d²s/dt² = 6t − 12, which equals 6 at t = 3. −6 m/s² is the acceleration at t = 1.

questions.s: The limit of (sin 3x)/x as x → 0 is
questions.e: Write sin 3x/x = 3 · sin 3x/(3x), which tends to 3 × 1 = 3. The answer 1 treats the standard limit as if the factor 3 were absent.

questions.s: The value of the integral of (x + 1)² from x = 0 to x = 1 is
questions.e: [(x + 1)³/3] from 0 to 1 = (8 − 1)/3 = 7/3. 8/3 uses only the upper limit.

questions.s: The greatest possible area of a rectangle inscribed in a circle of radius 5 cm is
questions.e: The rectangle's diagonal is the diameter 10 cm. With sides x and y and x² + y² = 100, the area xy is greatest when x = y = 5√2, giving 50 cm². 100 is the diagonal squared, which is not an area of the rectangle.

questions.s: For f(x) = x⁴ at x = 0, which statement is true?
o: f′(0) = 0 and f has a minimum there
f has a point of inflection there
questions.e: f′(x) = 4x³ is 0 at x = 0, and f(x) ≥ 0 elsewhere, so there is a minimum even though f″(0) = 0. A zero second derivative does not guarantee an inflection point.

questions.s: The distance between the points (1, 2) and (4, 6) is
questions.e: d = √[(4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²] = √(9 + 16) = 5. 7 adds the differences instead of using the square root, and 25 forgets the root.

questions.s: The midpoint of the line segment joining (2, −4) and (6, 8) is
questions.e: Average the coordinates: ((2 + 6)/2, (−4 + 8)/2) = (4, 2). (8, 4) is the sum of the coordinates without halving.

questions.s: The slope of the line through the points (1, 3) and (3, 7) is
questions.e: m = (7 − 3)/(3 − 1) = 4/2 = 2. ½ inverts the ratio and 4 forgets to divide by the change in x.

questions.s: If a = (2, 3) and b = (1, −1), then a + b is
questions.e: Add the components: (2 + 1, 3 + (−1)) = (3, 2). (1, 4) is a − b.

questions.s: The dot product of the vectors (1, 2, 3) and (4, −5, 6) is
questions.e: (1)(4) + (2)(−5) + (3)(6) = 4 − 10 + 18 = 12. 32 results from ignoring the negative sign of −5.

questions.s: The magnitude of the vector 3i + 4j is
questions.e: |v| = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5. 7 adds the components without squaring.

questions.s: The slope of the line 2x + 3y = 6 is
questions.e: Solve for y: y = −(2/3)x + 2, so the slope is −2/3. 2/3 loses the sign when moving 2x to the other side.

questions.s: Two distinct non-vertical lines are parallel when their slopes are
questions.e: Parallel lines have the same inclination, hence equal slopes. Negative reciprocals describe perpendicular lines.

questions.s: The unit vector in the direction of (3, 4) is
questions.e: Divide by the magnitude √(9 + 16) = 5. Dividing by 7 (the sum) or 25 (the square) does not give length 1; (4/5, 3/5) points in a different direction.

questions.s: The y-intercept of the line y = 2x − 7 is
questions.e: Put x = 0: y = −7. 7 loses the sign, and 2 is the slope.

questions.s: The eccentricity of a parabola is
questions.e: A parabola is the conic whose distance from the focus equals the distance from the directrix, so e = 1. e = 0 belongs to a circle.

questions.s: The centre of the circle (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 16 is
questions.e: Compare with (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: h = 3 and k = −2. (−3, 2) wrongly reads the signs directly from the brackets.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (2, 3) with slope −1 is
questions.e: y − 3 = −1(x − 2) gives y = −x + 5, i.e. x + y = 5. x − y = −1 is the line through (2, 3) with slope +1.

questions.s: The distance of the point (1, 2) from the line 3x + 4y − 10 = 0 is
questions.e: d = |3(1) + 4(2) − 10|/√(3² + 4²) = 1/5. Forgetting to divide by √(a² + b²) = 5 gives 1.

questions.s: The equation of the circle with centre (1, −2) and radius 3 is
questions.e: Use (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² with h = 1, k = −2 and r² = 9. Writing 3 on the right-hand side forgets to square the radius.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola x² = 12y is
questions.e: Compare x² = 4ay: a = 3, and the focus on the y-axis is (0, a) = (0, 3). (3, 0) belongs to y² = 12x.

questions.s: The foci of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1 are
questions.e: For a hyperbola c² = a² + b² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5 and the foci lie on the x-axis at (±5, 0). (±√7, 0) uses a² − b², which is the ellipse formula.

questions.s: The angle between the vectors (1, 0) and (1, 1) is
questions.e: cos θ = (1·1 + 0·1)/(1 · √2) = 1/√2, so θ = 45°. 90° would need a zero dot product.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6) is
questions.e: The triangle has base 4 and height 6, so the area is ½ × 4 × 6 = 12. 24 forgets the ½.

questions.s: The equation of the line through (1, 2) perpendicular to 2x − y = 3 is
questions.e: The given line has slope 2, so the perpendicular has slope −½: y − 2 = −½(x − 1), i.e. x + 2y = 5. 2x − y = 0 also passes through (1, 2) but is parallel to the given line.

questions.s: The point that divides the segment joining (1, 2) and (7, 8) internally in the ratio 1 : 2 is
questions.e: The point is ((2·1 + 1·7)/3, (2·2 + 1·8)/3) = (3, 4), which is closer to the first point. (5, 6) uses the ratio 2 : 1.

questions.s: If a = (1, 2, 3) and b = (2, 0, 1), then a × b is
The vectors (1, 2, −1) and (2, k, 3) are perpendicular when k equals
questions.e: The dot product must be zero: 2 + 2k − 3 = 0, so k = ½. k = 2 would give a dot product of 3.

questions.s: The parabola y² = 4ax passes through the point (4, 4). Its focus is
questions.e: Substituting: 16 = 16a, so a = 1 and the focus is (a, 0) = (1, 0). The point (4, 0) is not related to the focus.

questions.s: The equation of the tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25 at the point (3, 4) is
questions.e: The tangent at (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = r², so 3x + 4y = 25. 4x + 3y = 25 does not even pass through (3, 4).

questions.s: The line y = x + c touches the circle x² + y² = 8 when c equals
questions.e: The distance from the origin to x − y + c = 0 must equal the radius: |c|/√2 = 2√2, so |c| = 4. 2√2 is the radius, not c.

questions.s: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y = 5 and 3x + 4y = 15 is
questions.e: The distance is |c₁ − c₂|/√(a² + b²) = 10/5 = 2. 10 forgets the division by √(a² + b²).

questions.s: The scalar projection of the vector (3, 4) on the vector (1, 1) is
questions.e: Projection = (a · b)/|b| = 7/√2. 7 forgets to divide by |b| = √2, and 7/2 divides by |b|² instead.

questions.s: The eccentricity of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1 is
questions.e: Here a² = 25, b² = 16, so c² = 9, c = 3 and e = c/a = 3/5. 4/5 uses b/a instead of c/a.

questions.s: The length of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = 12x is
questions.e: For y² = 4ax the latus rectum has length 4a = 12. 3 is a itself, the focal distance.

questions.s: The asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1 are
questions.e: Setting the right-hand side to 0 gives y = ±(b/a)x = ±4x/3. y = ±3x/4 inverts b/a.

questions.s: The vectors a and b have magnitudes 3 and 4, and the angle between them is 60°. The magnitude of a + b is
questions.e: |a + b|² = 9 + 16 + 2(3)(4)cos 60° = 25 + 12 = 37. √13 is |a − b|, and 7 would need the vectors to point the same way.

questions.s: The locus of a point whose distance from (3, 0) is twice its distance from (−3, 0) is the curve
questions.e: Squaring (x − 3)² + y² = 4[(x + 3)² + y²] gives 3x² + 3y² + 30x + 27 = 0, i.e. x² + y² + 10x + 9 = 0. A sign error in the cross term gives the version with −10x.

questions.s: An ellipse has its foci at (±3, 0) and passes through the point (0, 4). Its equation is
questions.e: The distance from (0, 4) to each focus is 5, so the sum of focal distances is 10 = 2a and a = 5. Then b² = a² − c² = 25 − 9 = 16. The foci on the x-axis require the larger denominator under x².

questions.s: The scalar triple product a · (b × c) for a = (2, 0, 1), b = (1, 3, 0) and c = (0, 1, 4) is
questions.e: It equals the determinant with rows a, b, c: 2(12 − 0) − 0(4 − 0) + 1(1 − 0) = 24 + 1 = 25. Dropping the last term gives 24.

questions.s: The number of common tangents to the circles x² + y² = 4 and (x − 3)² + y² = 1 is
questions.e: The centres are 3 apart and the radii 2 and 1 add to 3, so the circles touch externally. Touching externally gives two direct tangents and one common tangent at the point of contact, so 3 in all. 4 applies only to circles that are separate.

questions.s: The length of a focal chord of the parabola y² = 8x that makes an angle of 60° with the x-axis is
questions.e: A focal chord inclined at θ has length 4a/sin²θ. With a = 2 and sin²60° = ¾, the length is 8/(¾) = 32/3. Using sin θ instead of sin²θ gives 16/√3.

questions.s: The lines of slope 1 that are tangent to the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 are
questions.e: A tangent y = mx + c to x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 needs c² = a²m² + b² = 25 + 9 = 34. Using a² − b² = 16 is the focal formula, not the tangent condition.

questions.s: A chord of the circle x² + y² = 16 passes through the point A(4, 0) on the circle. The locus of its midpoint is
questions.e: If M(x, y) is the midpoint, OM is perpendicular to the chord AM, so x(x − 4) + y² = 0, i.e. x² + y² − 4x = 0, a circle on OA as diameter. x² + y² = 4 is centred at the origin and does not pass through A.

questions.s: The circle that passes through (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6) has equation
questions.e: The circle through the origin has the form x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy = 0. The other two points give 16 + 8g = 0 and 36 + 12f = 0, so g = −2 and f = −3. The constant term must be 0 because the circle passes through the origin.

questions.s: The equation of the circle with its centre at the origin and radius 5 is
questions.e: A circle with centre (0, 0) and radius r is x² + y² = r², so r² = 25. x² + y² = 5 forgets to square the radius.

questions.s: The focus of the parabola y² = 8x is the point
questions.e: Comparing with y² = 4ax gives 4a = 8, so a = 2 and the focus is (a, 0) = (2, 0). (4, 0) wrongly takes a = 4.

questions.s: The cross product i × j of the unit vectors along the x- and y-axes is
questions.e: With the right-hand rule, i × j = k. j × i = −k, so reversing the order reverses the sign.

questions.s: The circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0 has centre and radius
questions.e: Complete the squares: (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25, so the centre is (3, −2) and the radius 5. 25 is r², not r.

questions.s: The area of the triangle with vertices (2, 1), (6, 3) and (4, 7) is
questions.e: Area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)| = ½|2(−4) + 6(6) + 4(−2)| = ½(20) = 10. 20 forgets the ½.

questions.s: The area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are the vectors (1, 2, 2) and (2, 0, 1) is
questions.e: a × b = (2·1 − 2·0, 2·2 − 1·1, 1·0 − 2·2) = (2, 3, −4), and its magnitude is √(4 + 9 + 16) = √29. 29 forgets the square root.

questions.s: The angle between the lines y = x and y = √3 x is
questions.e: The inclinations are 45° and 60°, so the angle between them is 60° − 45° = 15°. 60° is the inclination of the second line only.

questions.s: The points (1, 2), (3, 6) and (k, 10) are collinear when k equals
questions.e: The slope from the first to the second is 2, so (10 − 2)/(k − 1) = 2 gives k − 1 = 4, k = 5. k = 4 gives a slope of 8/3.

questions.s: The vectors (1, 2, 3), (2, 1, 0) and (1, λ, −3) are coplanar when λ equals
questions.e: Coplanar vectors have a zero scalar triple product: 1(−3 − 0) − 2(−6 − 0) + 3(2λ − 1) = 6 + 6λ = 0, so λ = −1. λ = 1 gives 12 instead of 0.

questions.s: The line y = 2x + c touches the parabola y² = 8x. The value of c is
questions.e: For y² = 4ax the line y = mx + c is tangent when c = a/m. Here a = 2 and m = 2, so c = 1. c = 2 uses a alone and c = 4 multiplies a by m instead of dividing.
